correctness.rationale: The outer conic is a P1 and two contact points admit exactly split/non-split forms. The dual chord condition gives t/s in {r,r^{-1}}, with r of n>=3 dividing q-chi, yielding complete cycles. The split/nonsplit coordinate descends via t -> t^(epsilon*q), and quotient by mu_n gives torus with q^m-epsilon^m rational polygon parameters. Frobenius on n vertices is affine k -> j+epsilon*q*k; exact cyclic/Kummer counting proves all fixed vertex distributions, including parity split in reflection case. The source verifier independently enumerates all rational chords for primes 3..23 and coset fixed points. The general proof is algebraic and covers arbitrary odd prime powers; finite tests alone are not used as proof.

originality.rationale: Full primary comparison found the known geometric closure and the previously published nonsplit q+1 rational-vertex case, which are explicitly excluded from independent novelty. The new joint statement determines, for every split/nonsplit double-contact pair and every extension, the Fq-stable *unoriented* cycle torus and the complete Frobenius fixed-vertex distribution, including reflection cases with 0/1/2 rational vertices. None of the inspected published results states or implies the complete arithmetic distribution with the required extra Galois descent; priority remains provisional against other unindexed general torus-descent literature.
residual_risks: Other finite-field polygon papers may describe the split conic pencil in equivalent cyclic group language and implicitly imply some of the new formulas.
The 2020 nonsplit rational polygon existence/count is already established; this part is only incorporated as a baseline in a wider theorem.
Complete priority cannot be certified because not all historical and unpublished mathematical material is indexed.
Unindexed general torus-isogeny/Galois descent literature may supply equivalent or stronger results.

value.rationale: The distinction between an Fq-defined Poncelet cycle as a zero-dimensional finite étale polygon set and an all-Fq-rational-vertex polygon is a natural arithmetic gap not resolved by geometric porism. The claim completes the split and nonsplit double-contact families for all lengths and all field extensions, with a sharp rotation/reflection trichotomy and complete class frequencies, rather than a routine n=3 specialization. It exposes rational geometric polygons with no rational vertices and rigid one- or two-vertex descent.
